easy.def: To glide on ice or the ground with special shoes.

more.def: To glide over ice or smooth ground on wheels or blades attached to your shoes.
examples: We skated on the frozen pond.
The kids skated down the sidewalk.

easy.def: A boot with a blade or wheels on the bottom.

more.def: A shoe with a metal blade or wheels on the bottom for gliding.
examples: She laced up her ice skates.
He wore roller skates on the smooth path.
My skate got stuck in a crack.

easy.def: All the bones in a body.
examples: A fish has a skeleton too.
We saw a skeleton in science class.

more.def: The frame of bones that supports the body of a person or animal.
examples: The museum has the skeleton of a huge dinosaur.
The human skeleton has more than two hundred bones.
We found the skeleton of a small bird in the woods.
She drew a sketch of a bird.

more.def: A quick drawing that is not finished in detail.
examples: I made a quick sketch of the dog.
The artist's sketch was done in pencil.
She drew a sketch of the lake.

more.def: To make a quick, rough drawing.
examples: I sketched the old barn in my notebook.
She sketched the view from the window.
He sketched a picture of the horse.

easy.def: A long, thin board you wear on each foot to slide on snow.
examples: I wear skis in the snow.
The skis are on the rack.

more.def: One of two long, thin boards that are fastened to boots for sliding over snow.
examples: I strapped my skis onto my boots.
One ski slid away down the hill.
The skis left two tracks in the snow.

easy.def: To slide over snow on long boards.

more.def: To glide over snow on a pair of long, narrow boards.
examples: We ski in the mountains every winter.
He skied across the snowy field.

easy.def: Being able to do something well.
examples: She has great skill at soccer.

more.def: The ability to do something well, which you get from practice.
examples: She has great skill at playing the piano.
Reading is a skill that gets better with practice.

easy.def: The outside covering of your body.
examples: The sun can burn your skin.

more.def: The outer covering of the body of a person or animal.
examples: Put on sunscreen to protect your skin.
A snake sheds its skin as it grows.
Her skin felt warm in the sun.

easy.def: The outside layer of a fruit.
examples: Peel the skin off the banana.

more.def: The outer covering of a fruit or vegetable.
examples: Peel the skin off the orange.
The banana skin was brown and soft.
The tomato skin split in the heat.

more.def: Very thin, with little fat or flesh.
examples: A skinny branch snapped in the wind.
The skinny puppy needed more food.

more.def: To move forward with light hops from one foot to the other.
examples: The children skipped down the sidewalk.

more.def: To leave something out or not do it.
examples: Skip the hard question and come back to it.
He skipped breakfast and ran to the bus.

easy.def: Clothing that hangs down from your middle.

more.def: A piece of clothing that hangs from the waist and covers part of the legs.
examples: She wore a blue skirt to school.
The dancer's skirt twirled as she spun.
A skull is made of bone.

more.def: The set of bones that forms the head and protects the brain.
examples: The museum has a dinosaur skull.

easy.def: The space above us where we see clouds and stars.

more.def: The space above the Earth that we see when we look up.
examples: The sky turned orange at sunset.
A kite danced in the windy sky.
Stars fill the sky on a clear night.
